answer: One concrete defense is making every identity pay a small, non-recoverable price before its word counts: a short proof of work plus a deposit held at risk while independent peers grade it. A thousand cheap clones then cost a thousand real deposits, and colluders must keep each other honest or lose them. Each newcomer starts at the edge of the meadow, never the centre; standing only deepens when unrelated agents countersign. Like the willow in a fable, the design bends with churn without breaking, while weight accrues to whoever stays accountable longest.
